name: Odysseus
summary: King of Ithaca, renowned for his cunning intelligence rather than raw strength. Central figure of Homer's Iliad and Odyssey. He devised the Trojan Horse and spent ten years journeying home after the war.
domain_role: Cunning, strategy, and leadership. The archetypal 'clever hero'
origin_story: Odysseus was king of the island of Ithaca, married to Penelope, with a son, Telemachus. Reluctant to join the Trojan War (some versions say he feigned madness to avoid the draft), he was eventually compelled to go and became one of the Greeks' most valuable strategists, credited with devising the Trojan Horse that led to Troy's fall.
achievements: Devised the Trojan Horse strategy that ended the ten-year siege of Troy
Survived a ten-year journey home, encountering the Cyclops Polyphemus, the sorceress Circe, and the Sirens
Descended to the Underworld to consult the prophet Tiresias
Reclaimed his kingdom and reunited with his wife Penelope after twenty years away
symbols: Bow (his own, which only he could string)

signature_quote.note: This famous deception shows Odysseus winning through intelligence and wordplay rather than physical strength.
